summary: Greece's police yearbook gives known offenders of each offence by Greek or foreign citizenship (rape, homicide, domestic violence), but no victim tables and no child-specific offences. EKKA's referral mechanism reports child trafficking victims by country of origin. No crime statistic records ethnicity or Roma identity.

nations.National (Hellenic Police, EKKA): Annual police statistical yearbook; National Referral Mechanism report.

european_title: Not recorded by any Greek crime source
european_note: The yearbook's 'ethnikotita' (nationality) column distinguishes only Greek nationals from foreigners. No Greek crime, victim or child-protection statistic records ethnicity, so neither ethnic Europeans nor Roma identity can be measured.
proxy_note: Greece records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

breakdown.why: The Hellenic Police 2025 statistical yearbook (table 26) gives known offenders by Greek/foreign citizenship: rape 417 (148 foreign); offences against sexual freedom 1,443 (427 foreign). All victim ages; no child-specific offence and no victim tables. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Offenders under the domestic violence law: 23,248 known offenders (3,697 foreign); bodily harm 6,981 (1,557 foreign). All victim ages; no child victims. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Intentional homicide: 370 known offenders, 92 foreign citizens, all victim ages. No victims by age or citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

EKKA's National Referral Mechanism 2025 report gives 881 new presumed victims, 108 of them children, by country of origin: 24 Greek, 71 from African and 13 from Asian countries. Traffickers appear only within the personal-liberty chapter of the police yearbook (1,525 of 10,533 offenders foreign). Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Child pornography is inside the sexual-freedom chapter (427 of 1,443 offenders foreign). No victims by citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Greece scores 9% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. The Hellenic Police yearbook gives known offenders of each offence by Greek/foreign citizenship but has no victim or child-specific tables; EKKA reports child trafficking victims by country of origin. No ethnicity is recorded.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.

yb.name: Στατιστική επετηρίδα έτους 2025 (Statistical yearbook 2025)
yb.publisher: Ελληνική Αστυνομία / Υπουργείο Προστασίας του Πολίτη (Hellenic Police, Ministry of Citizen Protection)
yb.records: Recorded offences, solved offences and known offenders by offence and Greek/foreign citizenship; arrests by citizenship.
yb.limitations: Citizenship only; no victim tables; no child-specific offences. astynomia.gr returned Access Denied to the box; the identical file was taken from the ministry's own data.gov.gr dataset.

ekka.name: Ετήσια Έκθεση Εθνικού Μηχανισμού Αναφοράς 2025 (National Referral Mechanism annual report)
ekka.publisher: Εθνικό Κέντρο Κοινωνικής Αλληλεγγύης (EKKA, National Centre for Social Solidarity)
ekka.records: 881 new presumed trafficking victims (108 children) by sex, age, country of origin, residence status and exploitation.
ekka.limitations: Country of origin by region for children; presumed victims; no trafficker data.

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
